thread:
carmen: Brainstorm: pricing page experiment that's less 'calculator' and more of a 'path chooser' for developer vs platform teams. Could reduce confusion about tiers and surface recommended bundles.

mike: interesting. how would it differ from the current slab calculator?

carmen: two inputs only: team type (Developer / Platform / Enterprise) and expected monthly token volume. Output: recommended tier, ballpark monthly cost, and a short rationale. CTA changes based on team type (dev -> start free, platform -> get best practices guide, enterprise -> contact sales).

nina: good call. localization still required. also think we should A/B test the 'rationale' copy vs no rationale to see if it increases confidence.

sam: front-end scope seems small. the 'rationale' could be a 1-line sentence derived from mappings. ETA 3 days including tests.

kevin: routing rule: if recommended tier = Enterprise OR user chooses Enterprise, route to enterprise queue. Otherwise route to self-serve. Also include tag: recommended_tier, chosen_team_type.

mike: copy options for rationale: Variant A: "Recommended because your token volume fits our Pro slab and you get better throughput/gpu pricing." Variant B: "Recommended for teams wanting predictable throughput and priority support."

olivia: marketing ops: add utm_campaign=tier_pathchooser_q2 and track referral source. Also good webinar tie-in  could mention webinar replay in the results for platform teams.

marketing-bot: Heads-up: Product launch calendar has "Tier simplification" workstream on 2026-05-20. Coordinate so we don't clash.

carmen: timeline: copy + mapping today, eng ticket + analytics tomorrow, QA in 5 days, soft-launch next week to 30% of traffic. Run 10-day test.

sam: I'll create an analytics spec with events: pathchooser_open, pathchooser_submit, pathchooser_cta_click, pathchooser_followup_click.

kevin: sales ops: will provide recommended_tier->sales_queue mapping and sample payload.

mike: will draft the short rationale variations and the experiment plan (metrics: recommended->cta rate, lead quality, trial starts).

carmen: one more ask  add a small 'Why trust this estimate?' link that opens a modal with methodology (simple bullets). QA to check copy.

olivia: will prepare localization strings and a small UX test with non-technical participants.

carmen: thanks everyone. checklist: mapping, copy, analytics, routing, translations. ping when ready. :sparkles:
